subject: tu:game/movie/movieplayer
value:
ON A TU WHOSE FUNCTIONS ARE ALREADY INSTRUCTION-COUNT-EXACT, THE CORRECT TRACTABILITY RANKING IS regnorm's (STRUCTURAL + unpaired) WORD COUNT, AND `real` ACTIVELY MISRANKS IT -- BY A FACTOR THAT INVERTS THE WORK ORDER. Run the census before choosing a target; it is one regnorm call per function and it is the difference between working the right function and the wrong one.

MEASURED on movieplayer.cpp's 17 open functions 2026-09-01. Ranked by regnorm words, cheapest first: fn_800DBE98 0 STRUCT/0 unpaired; fn_800D87FC 1/0; fn_800D8F28 1/0; fn_800DA60C 0/2; fn_800DACD8 0/2; __ct__11MoviePlayerFv 0/2; fn_800D9C5C 1/2; fn_800D91B4 2/2; fn_800D8BCC 3/2; DTextInitColorRamp 5/1; fn_800D96B0 1/6; dtor_800DBB94 6/2; fn_800D86C8 2/10; fn_800D860C 0/14; fn_800D8784 3/12; fn_800DB3D4 3/14; PlayVQMovie 11/24.

THE INVERSION, which is the point. fn_800D87FC carries the roster's LARGEST real (232) and was the lane's designated hard target, described in its own superseded record as 'a genuine dead end pending a mechanism nobody has proposed yet' -- yet it is 1 STRUCTURAL word and 0 unpaired, i.e. ONE word from a pure recolor, with 116 renamings behind it. fn_800D8F28 (real 110) is likewise 1/0 with 54 renamings. Meanwhile fn_800D860C, at real 30 the second-CHEAPEST function by `real` and the one a real-ordered queue picks first, is 0 STRUCT but 14 unpaired -- a genuine schedule rewrite and much the harder job. A `real`-ordered or size-ordered queue therefore works these three in exactly the wrong order. Neither `--ops` nor `real` can see this: both fn_800D87FC and fn_800D860C report instruction-count parity, and fn_800D860C reports opcode multiset IDENTICAL, the strongest possible --ops verdict.

WHY THE RANKING IS THE RIGHT ONE: a function at 0 STRUCTURAL / 0 unpaired is webfrank-eligible and closes to real 0 as a recolor regardless of how large its `real` is, so (STRUCT + unpaired) is literally the remaining source-work debt while `real` is a downstream register-naming echo of it. This is the operational form of claim.law.closing-the-last-non-register-word-unlocks-a-full-recolor-rule: the census FINDS that law's population instead of stumbling on it.

TWO ARBITER CAVEATS, both hit in this census and both cheap to honour. (1) regnorm's CLEAN-RENAMING is not sufficient: fn_800DBE98 reports 0/0 CLEAN-RENAMING and webfrank_audit REJECTS it ('+0x3c: use of f0 does not correspond to f2 under the running renaming'), exactly the FPR case claim.law.declaration-order-numbers-the-registers consequence (1) predicts. Always run webfrank_audit on a 0/0 candidate before believing it. (2) regnorm's reported offsets are its own paired-sequence positions, NOT function-relative byte offsets: its UNPAIRED rows for fn_800DACD8 printed @0x1e4/@0x1e0 while the instructions actually live at 0x18c/0x188 in the aligned view. Locate the named instruction by grepping the fnasm listing for its text, never by pasting a regnorm offset into fnasm.

COROLLARY, a slotdiff census is worth running FIRST and is usually a fast NEGATIVE: all 17 functions returned frame-identical and SLOT MAP IDENTICAL, so the do_enemy_move-class frame error that the EN law found in enemy.c is absent TU-wide here. That negative is what makes the regnorm reading trustworthy, and it cost one pass.

CENSUS EXTENSION to claim.LZ_copy-form-taxonomy-and-payoff-inversion's FINDING 1, which enumerated only sites where BOTH sides decode as the same copy rD<-rS. fn_800D8F28@0xec is an addi_copy->mr pair with MATCHING DESTINATION and DIFFERING SOURCE (ours `addi r26,r28,0`, target `mr r26,r27`), a category that census did not count because the differing source is precisely what the recolor stage exists to fix. It is the first known member of a class that a COMPOSED equivalent_copy_form + recolor rule would reach and that no single-stage rule can: the form stage's documented `unconditional` mode requires the same rD<-rS and its per-word assert requires the rewrite to reach the target word, both of which fail pre-recolor. Recorded as a concrete rule-ordering question for whoever owns webfrank, NOT acted on: broadening the class is forbidden by the tool's own constraints.
